answer: A healthy habit I have developed over the past couple of years is going for a brisk walk every evening. I usually head down to the embankment along the Jamuna, not far from our flat, and walk for about forty minutes as the sun goes down. I started it during a stressful period when I needed a way to clear my head, and it quickly became a daily ritual. At the time, I was working long hours and hardly moving at all, and I could feel it affecting both my energy and my mood. What I love about it is that it is so simple yet genuinely [[beneficial]], both physically and mentally. After a long day at a desk, the fresh air and movement are wonderfully [[refreshing]]. It has noticeably improved my mood and helps me sleep far better at night. Sometimes my younger sister joins me, and we end up having the kind of relaxed conversations we rarely have at home. Honestly, this small habit has had a surprisingly [[profound]] effect on my overall wellbeing. I think habits like this are important because they are sustainable; unlike intense workouts, a daily walk is something you can [[sustain]] for years. It requires no equipment or gym membership, just a bit of consistency. I would genuinely recommend it to anyone. It has become one of the most valuable parts of my daily routine, and I would find it hard to give up now, especially on calm evenings when the river looks so [[tranquil]].

followUps.q: Do you still walk during the monsoon?
followUps.answer: Not always. When it is pouring, I sometimes walk up and down the stairs of our building instead, which my neighbours find rather amusing. But I try not to let the weather become an excuse.

followUps.q: Do you prefer walking alone or with someone?
followUps.answer: Mostly alone, because it gives me time to think things through. That said, walks with my sister or a friend are lovely too; they are just more about conversation than quiet [[reflection]].

note: Set the walk by the Jamuna, added why he started and his sister joining; replaced plain 'maintain' with [[keep up]] and added [[tranquil]].
